doc.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022

title: Jazz in academia, teaching and restaurant music idea
summary: Why academia embraces jazz, what graduates do, his eighth graders, and an idea to pay restaurants to play jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I think academia needs money, they need people to come to school, and jazz has been, over the last sixty years, very popular with young musicians, this, that and the other, and the question has always been well if you graduate these people and they can play jazz what are they going to do? Because there’s never been enough opportunities for everybody to play. So I don’t know what they do. They seep over into doing other things and maybe they teach privately and maybe they play two nights a week instead of five, and maybe they play two times a month instead of ten. I’m not sure. I’m not sure. I don’t know. But I will say this, and I came home from my class today with these eighth graders feeling this way. I’m right. I’m right. These people can improvise, and once you get them improvising, even on a simple scale, they get excited. Now we haven’t got to the stage where I’ve been able to play some — I played Charlie Parker for them one time and I gave them the first page of “Now’s the Time” solo. Okay? Which is way over their head. But I gave it to them and we listened to that, and we listened to one or two choruses of Hank Mobley playing “This I Dig of You.” This was several weeks ago. But you only

have about forty-two minutes. So I really need a listening class. That would help these people to appreciate it more, I know. But back to your question, academia and jazz — I don’t know. I just don’t know. I don’t know. You don’t hear it out. Here’s something I’d love to do. I’d love to get somebody with a whole lot of money and if we go to McDonald’s and Wendy’s and all these fast food places and say I will pay all of your BMI, your Muzak funds for five years. Three years. You don’t have to pay. You’re paying thousands of dollars a year, I’m going to pay it. I’m going to dictate what music you’re going to play and I’m going to give you some samples, and you’re going to play jazz. You’re not going to play “Giant Steps,” you’re going to play Bill Evans and Oscar Peterson, trios, and we’re going to play people playing ballads and blues and swing stuff but not fast. Maybe some big bands, maybe not. And we’re going to put that into your system and we’re going to contract us for five years. At the end of three years I know you would tell the difference. People would go there for the music. Now, my wife and I go out to eat quite a bit because she can’t really cook anymore. And yesterday we were at a place in Louisville called Freddy’s. We drove fifteen miles to get there. And it seems today every restaurant we go in has to have at least one or two screaming kids [imitates child screaming]. Now I will say I don’t think Freddy’s had any music, but there are some places where the music is just awful I think. But jazz used to be played you know. I think Panera still plays jazz possibly. But academia and jazz — I think the people running the shows, the deans and so forth, they were never taught to improvise and they still think of jazz as being special, over there. And they admire the jazzers because they know their theory, they can play their theory and they can play with music, they can play without music, they’re a total musician.
Yeah and most of them can go and fill a spot in the symphony orchestra too.

Exactly. Exactly. Sure can, yeah. But still we don’t know what to do with them. We don’t know how they do what they do. I think every college, freshmen coming in, the first semester they all have to take an improv class. They have to learn to play “Mary Had a Little Lamb,” “Happy Birthday,” this, that and the other, learn the blues, play the blues scale, play on Volume 24 major and minor, take those scales and put them to use.
